docs.title: HArdware Dependability for Embedded Systems (HADES)
docs.text:
Welcome to the official documentation website for the HArdware Dependability for Embedded Systems (HADES) research group at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC-CNS).

HADES operates within the High-Performance Embedded Systems (HPES) laboratory in coordination with the SOftware Dependability for Embedded Systems (SODES) and Applications for Intelligent Dependable Embedded Systems (AIDES) research groups.

docs.title: 🎯 Mission & Overview
docs.text:
Modern high-performance embedded systems across automotive, avionics, and space industries are increasingly complex in both hardware and software. Across these domains, systems demand not only high performance, but also a strict set of non-functional properties related to dependability, safety, security, and reliability.

The HADES group develops novel hardware designs as well as their required low-level software support. Our designs range from Register Transfer Level (RTL) implementations for FPGAs and ASICs to emulation and simulation models.

The team consists of more than 20 researchers, including PhD students, engineers, and postdocs with established industrial and academic experience.

docs.title: 🔬 Core Research Lines
docs.text:
⚡ Performance & WCET
  • Guaranteed Performance: Facilitating Worst-Case Execution Time (WCET) computation and minimizing WCET bounds.
  • Energy Efficiency: Low power and energy consumption for battery-powered and space-constrained harsh environments.
🛡️ Functional Safety
  • Safety Standards: Compliance with ISO 26262 (Automotive), DO-254 (Avionics), and ECSS (Space).
  • Architectural Primitives: Diverse redundancy, timing predictability, reliability, and design-for-test.
🔒 Security & Post-Quantum
  • Cybersecurity Primitives: Ensuring data confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity.
  • Post-Quantum Crypto: Hardware support for next-generation post-quantum security algorithms.
🛰️ Reliability & Radiation Testing
  • Harsh Environment Testing: Fault injection, Single Event Effects (SEE) analysis, and beam irradiation (neutrons, protons, heavy ions).
🏎️ Novel Architectures & Accelerators
  • Heterogeneous Compute: Integrating GPUs, AI/ML/DL accelerators with time determinism and safety compliance.
💻 Hardware-Software Co-Design
  • Low-Level Software: Custom compilers, drivers, and runtime support to enable hardware acceleration features.

docs.title: Hardware IPs
docs.text: The HADES research group develops a suite of open-source Register Transfer Level (RTL) IP cores designed for timing verification, fault-tolerance, diversity monitoring, and safety-critical execution in high-performance embedded systems across space, automotive, and railway domains.

docs.title: 🛡️ Featured Hardware IP Cores
1. SafeSU – Safe Statistics Unit
docs.text:
The Safe Statistics Unit (SafeSU) is an RTL IP core that implements advanced mechanisms for multicore timing interference verification, validation, and monitoring. SafeSU has been integrated and validated in commercial space-grade RISC-V and SPARCv8 MPSoCs.

docs.title: 2. SafeTI – Safe Traffic Injector
docs.text:
The Safe Traffic Injector (SafeTI) unit acts as an AHB Master IP connected to the main AMBA bus. Controlled via APB registers, SafeTI performs a controlled set of bus transactions to AHB Slave RAM memory based on data descriptors configured at startup. It allows researchers to generate controlled bus traffic and measure multicore interference alongside processing cores and monitoring units.

docs.title: 3. SafeDE – Safe Diversity Enforcer
docs.text:
The Safe Diversity Enforcer (SafeDE) hardware module provides light-lockstep support using a non-intrusive and flexible hardware core. It preserves time staggering across cores running redundant threads, bringing enforced temporal diversity to avoid common cause failures (CCFs) in safety-critical systems.

docs.title: Software & Tools
docs.text: The HADES research group develops specialized software libraries, compiler toolchains, and runtime environments to support fault tolerance, real-time predictability, and software-level diverse redundancy on high-performance embedded systems.

docs.title: 💻 Software Libraries & Tooling
1. SafeSoftDR – Safe Software Diverse Redundancy Library
docs.text:
The Safe Software Diverse Redundancy library (SafeSoftDR) provides programmers with a structured software interface to enable software diverse redundant execution within user-defined functions. SafeSoftDR allows critical embedded software applications to achieve fault tolerance and time/algorithmic diversity across processing cores without requiring dedicated hardware redundancy.
